text: Writing a full class with enter and exit just for a context manager is often overkill.
The contextmanager decorator lets you build one from a single generator function instead.
Everything before the yield is the setup, and everything after it is the cleanup.
[chuckle] So this tag manager prints an opening tag, yields to your code, then prints the closing tag.
The with block runs in the middle, perfectly bracketed by the setup and teardown.
[sniff] contextlib also ships handy ready-made managers, like suppress.
suppress quietly ignores specific exceptions, replacing a clunky try-except-pass block.
[sigh] Here a missing file no longer crashes us — the error is swallowed and the program continues.
[groan] contextlib turns context managers from a chore into a one-line habit worth reaching for often.
